subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module for a static pickup truck model, roughly 5.4m long and 2m wide, built from box geometries, making sure the lowest points rest properly at ground level.

I'm sketching the layout: chassis, underbody, cab and bed sections along the z-axis, with a matte gunmetal body offset by neon magenta, cyan, and warning yellow accents, plus a glowing cyan glass tint. I'm defining the underbody slab, lower body sides, and hood as separate boxes positioned along the frame.

Now I'm roughing out the cab, windshield, and bed geometry -- sloped front panels, tilted glass, roof slab, side windows, bed walls and tailgate -- then adding militarized cargo like a turret pedestal, twin barrels, roll bar, and roof light bar.

I'm also adding armor plates, bull bar, neon headlights, and chevron bumper stripes, plus designing the four hover thruster pods at each wheel position with glowing ring details.

Now I'm working out the pod vents, support arms, and wide stance spacing, then adding the two rear main thrusters as rotated cylinders with glowing discs at the back.

I'm importing the glow helper and adding an underglow strip plane along the body sides, setting up mirrored loops for left/right symmetry, then calculating the windshield's tilt angle and dimensions from hood to roof.

Now I'm working out the hood slope angles and positioning so the hood front dips downward and meets the cab base cleanly.

Adding rear window, headlights, grille, bull bar, skid plate, and the gun turret with cylindrical base and barrels...

Now I'm layering on roof details: light bar, satellite dish, antennas with glowing tips, mirrors, door seams and handles, angular armor plating, a yellow flank stripe, neon accents, a hood emblem, and door-mounted "07" numbering built from boxes.

Writing box-geometry helper...
